summary.goal: Enhance Planner to support DOT Framework (Decomposition, Orchestration, Trajectories) with complexity estimation, language/domain tier detection, step/depth limits enforcement, acceptance criteria generation, and Tuner integration for adaptive learning.
summary.rationale: Current Planner produces flat plans with no complexity estimation. Research shows P(success) = (0.5)^(T/50min) - decomposition is critical for reliability. Language tiers (Python vs COBOL) create 68-point accuracy gaps. Planner needs to estimate complexity, enforce limits, and feed predictions to Tuner for accuracy tracking.
in_scope: Complexity estimation (hybrid: deterministic formula + LLM adjustment within +/-20%)
Language/domain tier detection (Tier S/A/B/C/D affecting budgets and model selection)
Step limits enforcement (max 15-20 steps per scope)
Depth limits enforcement (max 3 levels of sub-plans)
Tuner integration (read PlannerConfig, emit complexity estimates for accuracy tracking)
out_of_scope: Sub-plan execution in Forge (separate Forge enhancement)
Aggregation step type (DOT Phase 1, separate feature)

acceptance_criteria.description: Each step has complexity_estimate: { level, score, confidence, signals, recommendation }
Complexity score is deterministic formula, with optional LLM adjustment capped at +/-20%
Language tier detected from step scope/description (S/A/B/C/D)
Language tier multiplier applied to complexity score
Plans exceeding 15 steps per scope trigger decomposition warning
Plans exceeding 3 levels of sub-plan depth are rejected
Acceptance criteria can be structured (type: test/review/metric, validation: exists/schema/test/human)
Planner reads PlannerConfig from Tuner on startup (graceful fallback)
Complexity weights from PlannerConfig are applied to estimation formula
Complexity estimates are included in published plan for Forge/Tuner consumption
Steps have optional task_contract: { inputs, outputs, done_definition }
API endpoint validates contracts at plan creation

observations: Current Step schema has: step_id, title, scope, description, dependencies, owner_role, acceptance_criteria, gate, sub_plan_id
Need to add: complexity_estimate (calculated), contract (optional), language_tier (detected)
sub_plan_id exists but is not enforced for depth limits
AcceptanceCriterion currently has { id, description, type? } - needs extension for validation
PlanVersion needs decomposition_config for limits enforcement
Tuner emits PlannerConfig with complexity_weights and decomposition thresholds
concerns: LLM adjustment: when to invoke LLM vs. pure deterministic? (Suggestion: only when score is 30-60, borderline)
Language detection: need heuristic based on file extensions in scope, keywords in description
Tuner cold start: use research-backed defaults until Tuner available

observations: MultiPL-E: Python 80% vs COBOL 12% = 68-point gap due to training data distribution
Six Sigma Agent: 5-agent voting on atomic steps = 43x reliability improvement
Solving Million-Step LLM: Zero errors with hierarchical decomposition
Research recommends: max 15-20 steps/scope, max 3 depth levels

summary.goal: Compute complexity estimates for each step using deterministic formula with optional LLM adjustment

acceptance_criteria.description: estimateComplexity(step) returns ComplexityEstimate with level, score, confidence, signals, recommendation
Score formula: descTokens/500*30 + scopeCount*10 + depCount*5 + acCount*3 + keywordBoost
Level mapping: <15=trivial, <30=simple, <50=moderate, <75=complex, else=very_complex
Recommendation: <30=proceed, <60=consider_decomposition, else=require_decomposition
Language tier multiplier applied: score * tier_multiplier
Optional LLM adjustment for borderline scores (30-60), capped at +/-20%
Confidence is 0.8 if historical data available, else 0.5

summary.goal: Detect programming language tier and domain familiarity from step context

Domain familiarity adjustment: +25% for mobile, +100% for embedded, etc.

summary.goal: Enforce step count and sub-plan depth limits per decomposition config

validateSubPlanDepth(plan_id) traverses sub_plan_id chain, rejects if > max_depth
